newsitem.title: USA: Mercantile to acquire Roosevelt Financial.
newsitem.headline: Mercantile to acquire Roosevelt Financial.

text.p: Mercantile Bancorp Inc will acquire Roosevelt Financial Group Inc in a definitive merger agreement valued at $1.072 billion, the companies said.
Mercantile will deliver up to 13 million shares of its common stock at an exchange ratio of 0.4211 shares, or $22 in cash for each remaining share of Roosevelt common stock.
The acquisition will be a tax-free exchange for shareholders receiving stock, and will be accounted for as a purchase transaction, the companies said.
In connection with the purchase, Mercantile said it plans to repurchase up to seven million common shares.

Plans call for the merger, which is subject to the approval of Roosevelt shareholders and regulatory agencies, to be completed in mid-1997. Branch consolidation of the combined entities will occur in mid-1998, the companies said.
The acquisition announced Monday closely follows Mercantile's $855-million merger with Mark Twain Bancshares Inc, announced in October.
The Roosevelt deal will make Mercantile the largest financial institution in Missouri, it said.

Following completion of the deal, Roosevelt chief executive Stanley Bradshaw will head the combined mortgage operations of the two companies and join Mercantile's management executive committee reporting to Thomas Jacobsen, Mercantile's chairman, president and chief executive.

Roosevelt is a thrift holding company with $9 billion in assets based in St. Louis and operating 81 locations in Missouri, Kansas and Illinois. Mercantile is an $18.2-billion bank holding company also based in St. Louis. It has banks in Missouri, Iowa, Kansas, Illinois and Arkansas.
